answer: An applicant kernel signs one admission cipher, and no lone canyon may honor it: three canyon boards with separate stakes must countersign. Within a single epoch, a canyon's repeated signatures lock doubling stake — first base, then twice that, then twice again — forfeited whole if any kernel it passed proves fake. Stacking clones through one canyon burns through the doubling in that epoch alone, so an operator must win a different independent board for each clone, each bribe exceeding that board's entire locked stake; an honest kernel pays base for one signature.
